source.check: the Colebrook count read in the Irish News of 6 June 1964, cross-checked against the News-Letter report of 23 May that there would be no contest in Lisnaskea in 1961 (not this round).

note: Triennial election of Lisnaskea Rural District Council, polled Thursday 4 June 1964. One contest, for the Colebrook seat, the only contest for the council. The other thirty divisions were filled unopposed; the Impartial Reporter of 21 May 1964, p. 7, names every nominee by division, including one newcomer, Mr. James Lynch, for the vacant Rosslea seat (added 6 Nov 2026). Printed: 'Robinson 114 votes, Hurst 88 votes. The electorate was 235 and the total poll 204, including two spoiled votes.' Robinson, the official Unionist, had been selected at a delegates' meeting to replace Hurst, who opposed him as an Independent after about thirty years' membership. The report prints the division as 'Colebrooke'.
